mainTopic: How the words of the נזיר פסוק teach two things: a גזירה שוה with the כהן גדול about נגעים and זיבה, and that a נזיר may become impure to bury a מת מצוה.
overview: The גמרא keeps explaining why each word in the פסוק about a נזיר's relatives is needed. It says the word ולאמו is there for a גזירה שוה, as taught in a ברייתא of רבי. רבי says a נזיר may not become impure from his relatives' death, but he may become impure from their נגעים and זיבה. A קל וחומר already teaches that a כהן גדול may not become impure for his mother, so the word אמו in his section is free. That free word links him to the נזיר, so he has the same limited ban. The גמרא then asks for the source that a נזיר may become impure to bury a מת מצוה. A ברייתא shows that the נזיר's ban already covers every human dead body, so the words 'for his father and his mother' are free to allow a מת מצוה. A קל וחומר from the כהן גדול is rejected, because a נזיר brings a קרבן for his impurity. Finally, the idea that a נזיר may become impure for all other dead people is rejected by a קל וחומר from a כהן הדיוט.

steps.title: The word ולאמו is for a גזירה שוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the word ולאמו in the נזיר פסוק is needed for a גזירה שוה, following רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Or for his mother": this word is there for a גזירה שוה, the way רבי teaches it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the word ולאמו appears in the פסוק about the נזיר: it is needed for a גזירה שוה. It is also setting up the ברייתא of רבי that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes no word in the פסוק is extra. Instead of teaching a new relative, ולאמו serves as a link word for a גזירה שוה. The details of that link are given in רבי's ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Learning a law from one topic to another because the same word appears in both
According to what רבי (רבי יהודה הנשיא) teaches
"Or for his mother", a word in the נזיר פסוק

phrases.english: "Or for his mother" is for a verbal analogy,
phrases.notes: This word comes from the נזיר פסוק, במדבר 6:7.

phrases.english: according to the view of Rabbi.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the word-by-word explanation of the נזיר פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word ולאמו in the נזיר פסוק is used for a גזירה שוה.

steps.title: רבי: a נזיר is forbidden only in death, not in נגעים or זיבה
steps.stepSummary: רבי learns from "במותם" that a נזיר may not become impure from a relative's death, but may from their נגעים and זיבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי says, about a נזיר the פסוק says "when they die": he may not become impure from their death, but he may become impure from their נגעים and their זיבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא of רבי. First רבי sets out the rule for a נזיר: only death impurity from relatives is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word במותם ("when they die") limits the ban to death. Other impurities that come from relatives, like נגעים or זיבה, are not forbidden to a נזיר. This is the rule that will later be carried over to the כהן גדול.

keyTerms.meaning: "When they die"
Their צרעת (leprosy) impurity
Their impurity from a זב-type discharge
Becomes ritually impure

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi says:
Regarding a nazirite, "when they die": he may not become impure,
but he may become impure
for their leprosy and for their zav-emission.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the ברייתא that step 1 referred to.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נזיר is forbidden to become impure only from his relatives' death, not from their נגעים or זיבה.

steps.title: How do we know the same rule for a כהן גדול?
steps.stepSummary: רבי asks where we learn that a כהן גדול is also limited only to death impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: I only know this for a נזיר. From where do I know it for a כהן גדול?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי asks a question: the rule was learned for a נזיר, so how do we know it for a כהן גדול too?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק with במותם is only about a נזיר. The כהן גדול section does not say "when they die," so we need a source to apply the same limit to him.

keyTerms.meaning: I only know (this case) so far
The High Priest
From where (do we learn it)?

phrases.english: And I have only a nazirite;
from where do I know it for a High Priest?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין לִי אֶלָּא בְּנָזִיר בְּכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to extend step 2's rule to the כהן גדול.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that a כהן גדול, like a נזיר, is forbidden only in death and not in נגעים or זיבה.

steps.title: A קל וחומר shows אמו is not needed for the כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: רבי shows through a קל וחומר that the ban on a כהן גדול for his mother is known by logic, so the word אמו is not needed for that.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can say: the פסוק did not need to say "his mother" for the כהן גדול, because it is a קל וחומר. A regular כהן may become impure for his brother from his father, yet a כהן גדול may not become impure even for his father. So a regular כהן may not become impure for his brother from his mother. Isn't it logical that a כהן גדול may not become impure for his mother?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי begins his answer by showing that the word אמו in the כהן גדול section is not needed for its plain meaning. This sets up the next move: if it is not needed there, it is free for a גזירה שוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן הדיוט may become impure for a paternal brother, and still the כהן גדול may not even become impure for his father. The maternal side is weaker, since a כהן הדיוט may not become impure for a maternal brother. So the כהן גדול is surely forbidden for his mother, and we would know this even without the word.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument from a lighter case to a stricter one
A regular כהן
The פסוק has no need to say it
Isn't it logical?
His brother from the same mother only

steps.confusionAlert: This קל וחומר is not the final answer to the question. It only proves that the word אמו is extra, which opens the door to the גזירה שוה.

phrases.english: You can say: "his mother" need not be said about a High Priest,
phrases.notes: The כהן גדול פסוק is ויקרא 21:11.

phrases.english: for there is no need for the verse to say it,
since it is an a fortiori argument:
Just as in a case where a common priest
becomes impure for his paternal brother,
a High Priest does not become impure even for his father,
then in a case where a common priest does not
become impure for his maternal brother,
is it not logical that a High Priest does not
become impure for his mother?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַרְתָּ לֹא יֵאָמֵר אִמּוֹ בְּכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל שֶׁאֵין תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering step 3 by showing the word אמו for the כהן גדול is free.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: First stage of the answer: a קל וחומר proves the כהן גדול may not become impure for his mother, so the word אמו is extra.

steps.title: If logic teaches it, why does the verse say "his mother"?
steps.stepSummary: רבי asks: since the קל וחומר already proves it, what does the word אמו for the כהן גדול teach?
steps.simpleTranslation: If you learned it from logic, why does the פסוק say "his mother" about the כהן גדול?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי points out the problem the קל וחומר creates: the word אמו now looks unneeded. This sets up the answer that it is free for a גזירה שוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה does not write extra words. Since logic already gives the plain meaning, the word אמו must be there for something else.

keyTerms.meaning: If you succeeded in learning it from logic
Why does the פסוק say it?

phrases.english: If you have derived it from the logical argument,
why does the verse say "his mother" about a High Priest?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם זָכִיתָה מֵהַדִּין מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the consequence of step 4's קל וחומר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word אמו in the כהן גדול פסוק.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a קל וחומר already teaches its plain meaning, the word seems extra.

steps.title: The free word links the כהן גדול to the נזיר
steps.stepSummary: The word אמו is free, so it makes a גזירה שוה between the נזיר and the כהן גדול, where both say אמו.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is free, to compare and learn a גזירה שוה from it: "his mother" is said about a נזיר, and "his mother" is said about a כהן גדול.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי answers: the extra word אמו is free, so it creates a גזירה שוה with the same word in the נזיר פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה שוה works best when the linking word is not needed for anything else. Since the קל וחומר made אמו extra for the כהן גדול, it can link the two topics.

keyTerms.meaning: Free: not needed for its plain meaning, so available to teach something else
To compare
And to learn from it

phrases.english: It is free, to compare
and to learn a verbal analogy from it:
"His mother" is said about a nazirite,
and "his mother" is said about a High Priest.

steps.triggerLanguage: מוּפְנֶה לְהַקִּישׁ וְלָדוּן הֵימֶנּוּ גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 5 by giving the extra word a job.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the extra word to a גזירה שוה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word אמו for the כהן גדול looks pointless once the קל וחומר exists.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is מופנה and links the כהן גדול to the נזיר.

steps.title: Like a נזיר, a כהן גדול is forbidden only in death
steps.stepSummary: Through the גזירה שוה, the כהן גדול may not become impure from his relatives' death but may from their נגעים and זיבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as "his mother" said about a נזיר means he may not become impure from their death but may from their נגעים and זיבה, so too "his mother" said about a כהן גדול means he may not become impure from their death but may from their נגעים and זיבה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי finishes the גזירה שוה and gives the result: the כהן גדול has the same limited ban as the נזיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answers the question of step 3. The limit "only death", learned from במותם for the נזיר, now also applies to the כהן גדול. So נגעים and זיבה of his relatives are not forbidden to him.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as ... so too: the form of a comparison
That is said (in the פסוק)

steps.whatToRemember: ולאמו in the נזיר פסוק is used for רבי's גזירה שוה. Because the word אמו for the כהן גדול is free (a קל וחומר already teaches it), the two are linked. Both a נזיר and a כהן גדול are forbidden only in their relatives' death, not in their נגעים or זיבה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how a word made extra by a קל וחומר becomes available for a גזירה שוה, and it explains why the word ולאמו is needed in the נזיר פסוק.

phrases.english: Just as "his mother" stated about a nazirite:
in their death he may not become impure,
but he may become impure for their leprosy and their zav-emission,
so too "his mother" stated about a High Priest:
in their death he may not become impure,
but he may become impure for their leprosy and their zav-emission.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out what the גזירה שוה of step 6 teaches.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A כהן גדול, like a נזיר, is forbidden to become impure only from his relatives' death, not from their נגעים or זיבה.

steps.title: What is the source for the נזיר?
steps.stepSummary: We have a source for the כהן גדול. Now the גמרא asks for the source that a נזיר becomes impure for a מת מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We found the source for a כהן גדול. For a נזיר, where do we learn it from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the topic of a מת מצוה. It already has the source that a כהן גדול becomes impure for one, and now asks for the matching source for a נזיר. This sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both a כהן גדול and a נזיר are forbidden to become impure even for close relatives. The source that a כהן גדול may still bury a מת מצוה does not automatically cover a נזיר, so the גמרא needs a separate source.

keyTerms.meaning: We have found (a source for this)
From where do we learn it?
A dead body with no one else to bury it, which everyone must bury

phrases.english: We have found [the source for] a High Priest.
phrases.notes: He means the source that a כהן גדול becomes impure to bury a מת מצוה.

phrases.english: A nazir, from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves רבי's side point about נגעים and זיבה and returns to the main topic. The source that a כהן גדול becomes impure for a מת מצוה was already found earlier, so now the גמרא asks for the matching source for a נזיר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק source that a נזיר may become impure for a מת מצוה.

steps.title: The verse speaks of a human body, not an animal
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא shows that the נזיר's ban is about human dead bodies. An animal's body is not included.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'All the days he is a נזיר to ה׳, he shall not come upon a dead body.' I might think even an animal's body is included, since the תורה says 'one who strikes the נפש of an animal.' So the פסוק says 'a dead body,' which shows it means a human body.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. The ברייתא first shows that the נזיר's ban covers every dead human body, but not animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word נפש can mean an animal, so the ברייתא needs to show the פסוק means people. Once the פסוק covers all human dead, relatives included, the later words about father and mother become free to teach something new.

keyTerms.meaning: Body or living being. It can refer to a person or to an animal
I might have understood
The פסוק teaches (us otherwise)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't get lost because the פסוק is quoted twice. The first time it is just the starting quote. The second time the ברייתא is pointing to the wording of that same פסוק as the proof that it means humans.

phrases.english: As it is taught [in a baraita]:
"All the days he is a nazir to the Lord
he shall not come upon a dead body,"

phrases.aramaic: שׁוֹמֵעַ אֲנִי אֲפִילּוּ נֶפֶשׁ בְּהֵמָה בַּמַּשְׁמָע,
phrases.english: I would understand that even an animal's body is included,
as it is said elsewhere
"one who strikes the nefesh of an animal,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 24:18. Here the תורה uses נפש for an animal.

phrases.english: Therefore the verse teaches:
"he shall not come upon a dead body,"
the verse is speaking of a human body.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the question by bringing a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The נזיר's ban covers every human dead body. This prepares the ground for freeing up 'father and mother.'

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל proves it from the words 'shall not come'
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל says no special proof is needed. 'He shall not come' already shows the פסוק means a human corpse.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל says: that proof is not needed. The פסוק says 'he shall not come,' so it is speaking about bodies that make a person impure just by coming in.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל gives a different way to show the פסוק is about human bodies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a human corpse makes a person impure when he comes into the same tent with it. An animal carcass makes a person impure only by touching or carrying it. So 'he shall not come' can only mean a human body.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not needed
Coming in (entering a tent that has the corpse inside)
That make someone impure

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael says: It is not necessary,
for it says "he shall not come,"
[meaning] about bodies that make impure through coming in
phrases.notes: Only a human corpse makes you impure just by being under the same roof. An animal carcass has to be touched or carried.

phrases.english: is the verse speaking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reaches the same result as the previous step through a different word in the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'He shall not come' limits the פסוק to human corpses, which make a person impure through entering.

steps.title: Father and mother are excluded, but a מת מצוה is allowed
steps.stepSummary: All human dead are already forbidden, so 'for his father and mother' teaches that only for them is he forbidden. For a מת מצוה he may become impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'For his father and his mother' he may not become impure. But he does become impure for a מת מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives its answer: the words about father and mother teach that a נזיר may become impure for a מת מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since every human body is already forbidden, the תורה did not need to name relatives just to forbid them. The extra words teach a limit: he may not become impure for relatives, but he may for a מת מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: For his father and for his mother
Becomes ritually impure

steps.whatToRemember: A נזיר may not become impure even for his parents, but he must become impure to bury a מת מצוה. This is learned from the extra words 'for his father and his mother.'

phrases.english: "For his father and for his mother" he does not become impure,
phrases.notes: במדבר 6:7. All human dead are already covered, so these words are free to teach something new.

phrases.english: but he does become impure for a met מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the result of the last two steps, that all human dead are forbidden, to free the words 'father and mother' to teach something new.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A נזיר becomes impure for a מת מצוה, learned from the extra words 'for his father and his mother.'

steps.title: Why a פסוק? A קל וחומר from the כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks why a פסוק is needed. If a כהן גדול with permanent holiness may bury a מת מצוה, then surely a נזיר may too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even before the פסוק said it, I could figure it out with logic. If a כהן גדול, whose holiness lasts forever, becomes impure for a מת מצוה, then a נזיר, whose holiness does not last forever, should surely be allowed to become impure for a מת מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges its own answer. A קל וחומר from the כהן גדול seems to prove the rule without any פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן גדול is holy for his whole life, and a נזיר is holy only for a limited time. If the holier person may bury a מת מצוה, the less holy one should be allowed too. This makes the פסוק look extra, so the ברייתא needs to explain why it is still needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Even before (or without) it being said
I can figure it out by logic
Permanent holiness that lasts forever
Isn't it logical?

phrases.english: Even if it had not been said,
I could derive it by logic:
If a High Priest,
whose holiness is permanent,
becomes impure for a met מצוה,
a nazir, whose holiness is not permanent,
is it not logical that he becomes impure for a met מצוה?

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד שֶׁלֹּא יֵאָמֵר, יֵשׁ לִי בַּדִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the פסוק used in the previous step.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of 'for his father and his mother' as the source for a נזיר and a מת מצוה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר from the כהן גדול, whose holiness is permanent, already proves the rule for a נזיר, whose holiness is temporary. That makes the פסוק seem unnecessary.

steps.title: The קל וחומר from the כהן גדול is rejected
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rejects the קל וחומר from step 12. A כהן גדול brings no קרבן for his impurity, but a נזיר does. So maybe a נזיר is stricter and may not become impure even for a מת מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. You can say this about a כהן גדול, because he does not bring a קרבן for his impurity. Can you say the same about a נזיר, who does bring a קרבן for his impurity? Since he brings a קרבן for his impurity, maybe he should not become impure for a מת מצוה?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא pushes back on its own קל וחומר from step 12. It points to a way a נזיר is stricter than a כהן גדול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 argued: if the holier כהן גדול may bury a מת מצוה, then surely a נזיר may too. Here the ברייתא says a נזיר's impurity is treated more seriously, because it forces him to bring a קרבן. Because of this difference the קל וחומר breaks down, so we really do need a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (this about one case), can you say it about the other? The formula used to break a קל וחומר
An offering brought because he became impure
Since, because
An unattended dead body that no one else will bury, which must be buried

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the ברייתא is now ruling that a נזיר may not bury a מת מצוה. It is only showing that logic alone cannot prove it, so the next line brings a פסוק.

phrases.english: No: if you say this about a High Priest,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכֵּן אֵינוֹ מֵבִיא קׇרְבָּן עַל טוּמְאָתוֹ,
phrases.english: that is because he does not bring an offering for his impurity,

phrases.aramaic: תֹּאמַר בְּנָזִיר, שֶׁמֵּבִיא קׇרְבָּן עַל טוּמְאָתוֹ.
phrases.english: would you say it about a nazirite, who does bring an offering for his impurity?
Since he brings an offering for his impurity,
perhaps he should not become impure for a met מצוה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קל וחומר proposed in step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The קל וחומר from כהן גדול to נזיר
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A נזיר's impurity is more serious because it requires a קרבן, so he cannot be learned from a כהן גדול.

steps.title: The פסוק teaches he may become impure for a מת מצוה
steps.stepSummary: Since logic does not work, the פסוק 'for his father and mother he shall not become impure' is needed. It teaches that a נזיר may still become impure for a מת מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the פסוק says: 'For his father and for his mother he shall not become impure.' But he does become impure for a מת מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the קל וחומר has fallen, the ברייתא brings the פסוק as the real source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only father and mother are named as forbidden. That limit shows the ban does not reach a מת מצוה. This answers the question from step 8 and backs up the reading in step 11.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches; introduces the source from the Torah
'For his father and his mother he shall not become impure' (במדבר 6:7)

steps.whatToRemember: A נזיר may become impure to bury a מת מצוה. We learn it from the פסוק, not from a קל וחומר from the כהן גדול.

phrases.english: Therefore the verse says: "For his father and for his mother he shall not become impure,"
but he does become impure for a met מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the logical proof is rejected in step 13, the פסוק is given as the source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'for his father and mother' limit the ban, so a נזיר may become impure for a מת מצוה.

steps.title: Maybe he may become impure for all other dead
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests a different reading. Maybe the פסוק forbids only father and mother, and a נזיר may become impure for any other dead person.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe it means: he may not become impure for his father and mother, but he may become impure for other dead people!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises another possible way to read the same פסוק. This sets up the next step, which will reject it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If naming father and mother limits the ban, maybe it limits it completely. Then every other dead person, not only a מת מצוה, would be allowed. This would make the ban much smaller than we thought.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps; introduces another possible reading
Other dead people, not relatives

phrases.english: Or perhaps: he does not become impure for his father and mother,
but he may become impure for other dead people!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading in step 14 by offering a wider reading of the same פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'father and mother' allows only a מת מצוה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The limit to father and mother could just as well allow all other dead people.

steps.title: A קל וחומר from a כהן הדיוט rejects this
steps.stepSummary: A כהן הדיוט may become impure for relatives, yet he may not for other dead people. A נזיר may not become impure even for relatives, so surely he may not for other dead people.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can say a קל וחומר: a כהן הדיוט may become impure for his relatives, yet he may not become impure for other dead people. A נזיר may not become impure even for relatives. So isn't it logical that he may not become impure for other dead people?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא rejects the suggestion of step 15 using a קל וחומר from a regular כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A regular כהן is more lenient than a נזיר, since he may become impure for relatives. Even so, he is forbidden for other dead people. So the stricter נזיר must surely be forbidden for other dead people too. This leaves only the מת מצוה as allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Logic from a lighter case to a stricter case
A regular כהן, not the כהן גדול
Close relatives
Isn't it logical?

steps.whatToRemember: A נזיר is forbidden to become impure for any dead person, even his relatives. The only exception is a מת מצוה.

phrases.english: You can say a kal vachomer:
If a common priest, who becomes impure for relatives,
still does not become impure for other dead people,
then a nazirite, who does not become impure even for relatives,

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁלֹּא יִטַּמֵּא לִשְׁאָר מֵתִים?
phrases.english: is it not logical that he should not become impure for other dead people?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the wider reading proposed in step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that a נזיר may become impure for all other dead people
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It goes against a קל וחומר from a regular כהן, who is more lenient yet is still forbidden for other dead people.
